# RFC-0003: Server, Recipe, And Runtime Execution Contract

> **Version:** 0.15.0 | **Status:** normative | **Phase:** impl
> **Owners:** @Zihua Wu

---

## 1. Summary

### [RFC-0003:C-SUMMARY] Summary (Informative) <a id="rfc-0003c-summary"></a>

This RFC governs independently launchable servers, server-owned cases, recipes, and runtime execution: typed resolution before external effects, long-running and closed-loop lifecycles including image-backed launches, canonical Engine, Gateway, and P/D Router components, per-role parallelism, and fused P/D frontend binding. [RFC-0001](../rfc/RFC-0001.md) holds the specification overview and authority map.

*Since: v0.1.0*

---

## 2. Specification

### [RFC-0003:C-RECIPE-COMPOSITION] Server, Case, And Recipe Composition (Normative) <a id="rfc-0003c-recipe-composition"></a>

A server MUST be an independently launchable workspace definition. Its `stack`, `model`, and `topology` fields MUST select exactly one stack, model, and supported topology; its common behavior and canonical model-serving `roles` supply the typed base inherited by its cases.

A `single` topology MUST use the canonical model-serving role `serve`. When its server base declares `gateway_backend`, resolution MUST additionally derive the canonical frontend process role `gateway`; when it omits `gateway_backend`, resolution MUST derive no frontend process role. A `single` server MUST NOT declare `pd_router_backend`.

A `prefill_decode` topology MUST use canonical model-serving roles `prefill` and `decode`. Its server base MUST declare independently selected `gateway_backend` and `pd_router_backend` values. Resolution MUST derive one canonical `gateway` process role whose closed component binding contains both Gateway and P/D Router.

Workspace configuration MUST reject `roles.gateway`, `roles.pd_router`, `roles.router`, and every other authored frontend role. It MUST NOT permit alternate names for canonical roles or a public role `kind` field; topology and backend presence determine role identity and cardinality.

A server MAY define identifier-keyed `cases` and an optional `default_case`. Each case MUST be a typed behavior patch over that server. A case MUST NOT change the selected stack, model, topology, canonical role identities, case set, placement, model locator, presence of either frontend component, or canonical frontend process-role cardinality. An empty case is valid.

A declared `default_case` MUST reference one owned case. A server with no cases MUST resolve its base behavior when case selection is omitted and MUST reject `--case`. A server with exactly one case MUST select that case when case selection is omitted. A server with more than one case MUST declare a valid `default_case`; omission MUST select it. Explicit case selection MUST name one case owned by the selected server.

A recipe MUST select exactly one `server` and one `workload_suite`. It MUST NOT own, copy, filter, reorder, or redefine the server's cases.

A workload suite MUST name an ordered sequence of Eval and Bench measurements and MAY name one Eval as its gate. A gated Bench is skipped when the gate does not succeed ([RFC-0004:C-MEASUREMENTS](../rfc/RFC-0004.md#rfc-0004c-measurements)).

Every referenced model, stack, server, measurement, workload suite, and selected case MUST resolve within the selected workspace revision before the first external effect.

An ordinary operator MUST be able to select a server directly or select a recipe and, when applicable, one server case without manually composing referenced definitions.

A recipe MUST define bounded server-plus-measurement composition. The public contract MUST NOT require users to author arbitrary task nodes or a general workflow DAG.

**Rationale:** Server intent has an independent lifecycle and reuse boundary: the same server is started directly, consumed by multiple recipes, attached to a manual Bench, and referenced by image validation. Server-owned typed cases vary behavior without giving recipes a second authority. Fixed model-serving roles and one closed frontend process role let placement, records, and integrations share one vocabulary without turning topology into a general graph language. The server base fixes component presence and process cardinality while cases compare compatible Gateway and P/D Router backends independently.

*Since: v0.1.0*

### [RFC-0003:C-RESOLUTION] Resolution Dry Run And Overrides (Normative) <a id="rfc-0003c-resolution"></a>

Server resolution MUST use one ordered path: load the workspace; select the server, case, stack, and model; load the permitted local bindings and select placement; merge typed behavior patches; validate realization compatibility; invoke integration planning; allocate ranks, machine-specific model locators, ports, caches, and network facts; invoke final integration rendering; then freeze one immutable resolved execution object.

Behavior precedence MUST be server base, then the selected server case, then invocation-scoped overrides in command-line order. Resolution MUST preserve the ordered common and role declaration layers and the source of every effective behavior-affecting value.

The effective Gateway-backend and P/D-Router-backend identities MUST each be the corresponding backend identity after server-base, selected-case, and invocation-override precedence. They MUST remain separate facts even when they name the same provider or share one process.

For a `single` server, the base definition's `gateway_backend` presence MUST determine whether resolution derives the canonical `gateway` process role. A case or invocation-scoped override MAY replace the effective Gateway-backend identity only when the server base declares `gateway_backend`. It MUST NOT introduce or remove the Gateway component or introduce a P/D Router component.

For a `prefill_decode` server, the base definition MUST declare both backend fields. A case or invocation-scoped override MAY replace either effective backend identity independently. It MUST NOT introduce or remove either frontend component or change the one derived frontend process role.

An invocation-scoped override MUST use repeatable `--set <TOML-KEY-PATH>=<TOML-VALUE>`. TOML quoted key segments MUST allow a literal dot in a key. Values MUST be parsed as TOML values. Repeated overrides apply left to right, and the last assignment to the same path wins.

A `serve start` override path MUST be rooted at the selected server through `server`. A `recipe run` override path MAY be rooted at `server`, `evals.<eval-id>`, or `benches.<bench-id>` under [RFC-0004:C-RECIPE-MEASUREMENT-OVERRIDES](../rfc/RFC-0004.md#rfc-0004c-recipe-measurement-overrides). Framework setting paths MUST use `server.settings.<key>` for common values or `server.roles.<role>.settings.<key>` for role values. A core server field name MUST NOT be reinterpreted as a framework setting.

Cases and invocation overrides MUST use the same typed patch model. An override MAY change only typed server behavior fields and entries under an explicit framework `settings` map. It MUST NOT change server identity, stack, model, topology, canonical role identities, case definitions, case selection, placement, model locators, frontend-component presence or canonical frontend process-role cardinality.

Workspace server configuration MUST declare a positive framework-neutral `readiness_timeout_seconds` independently of framework settings. An integration response MUST NOT replace it. Ordinary launch readiness MUST be finite. Its owning budget MUST begin immediately after every resolved process has spawned and immediately before the first blocking process-status, HTTP-readiness, or target-registry attempt. A capture-armed launch waits without that owner budget under [RFC-0004:C-WORKLOAD-PROFILING](../rfc/RFC-0004.md#rfc-0004c-workload-profiling).

Workspace server configuration MUST also accept a positive framework-neutral `readiness_attempt_timeout_seconds`, defaulting to 30 seconds when undeclared. The value MUST bound each blocking process-status, HTTP readiness, and target-registry attempt during readiness; one HTTP attempt includes connection establishment and the complete response. For finite readiness, the effective attempt deadline MUST be the lesser of this value and the readiness owner’s remaining budget. Expiry of a blocking attempt MUST return control to the finite readiness loop and MUST NOT by itself terminate readiness. For capture-armed readiness, attempt expiry MUST return control to the unbounded readiness loop without making that loop terminal.

Server cases and invocation-scoped server overrides MUST be able to patch `readiness_timeout_seconds` through the typed server patch model.

Server cases and invocation-scoped server overrides MUST be able to patch `readiness_attempt_timeout_seconds` through that same typed server patch model. The frozen resolved server, dry-run, and record MUST preserve its effective value, and an integration response MUST NOT replace it.

A profiling-capable server MUST resolve positive `capture_arm_deadline_seconds`, `capture_control_deadline_seconds`, and `capture_finalization_deadline_seconds` facts. The arm and control budgets MUST default when undeclared to 60 seconds each. The finalization budget default MUST follow the resolved capture mechanism under [RFC-0004:C-WORKLOAD-PROFILING](../rfc/RFC-0004.md#rfc-0004c-workload-profiling): 300 seconds for managed collection and 3600 seconds for engine trace, whose stop dispatch, response consumption, and artifact flush wait share that one budget. Server cases and invocation-scoped server overrides MUST be able to patch all three through the typed server patch model. The frozen resolved server, dry-run, and record MUST preserve their effective values.

The selected realization MUST be validated against the resolved server before any state-affecting command. A local realization MUST use the server stack's Pixi environment. A built image MUST realize the same stack. A declared external image MUST carry an immutable digest and claim an integration compatible with the server stack; it does not claim stack equality.

Local integration operations MUST execute in the selected stack's Pixi environment. Image-backed integration operations MUST execute against the selected image realization. Integration operations and external probes used during resolution MUST be read-only.

The frozen resolved object MUST be the sole authority for dry-run output, state-affecting execution, cleanup, and record production. Execution MUST NOT reload configuration, reselect defaults, rerun placement choice, or reconstruct server, case, adapter, endpoint, command, or measurement facts after that object is frozen.

For an adaptive Bench, the frozen parent resolved object MUST own the complete effective definition, endpoint, immutable case inputs, SLOs, and adaptive policy.

Each outcome-dependent adaptive probe MUST be derived only from that frozen parent and the recorded prior case-level SLO evaluations, and MUST itself be frozen as one immutable child case execution object before its first external effect.

Adaptive child-case derivation MUST NOT reload workspace configuration, reapply overrides, or reconstruct a fact already frozen in the parent.

Dry-run MUST perform the same reference resolution, case selection, typed patching, placement compatibility, determinable resource and toolchain validation, integration planning and rendering, rank allocation, locator resolution, endpoint allocation, cache allocation, and command construction required before real execution. It MUST NOT launch a server, execute a measurement, acquire persistent server-operation ownership, execute realization checks, or create a record that claims execution occurred.

Manual Bench resolution MUST combine one named Bench definition from the discovered workspace root, one explicit running server record stored under that root, the immutable endpoint, model, and server-control capabilities in that record, the Bench toolchain owned by the invoking InferLab release, and invocation-scoped Bench overrides.

A manual Bench MAY use a newer or dirty measurement workspace snapshot than the serving snapshot. It MUST reject a target record whose record schema or preserved server capabilities are incompatible with the invoking release.

A manual Bench override MUST use repeatable `--set <path=value>`, patch the selected typed Bench definition in command-line order, and be fully validated before case expansion. It MUST NOT change Bench identity or kind, target server record, endpoint, model, serving integration, or local bindings.

A Bench that requests prefix-cache reset MUST fail preflight when the target server record does not preserve a compatible reset capability.

For a static Bench matrix, dry-run MUST report every exact expanded case in execution order and the resolved aggregate and request-level SLO inputs that apply to those cases.

For an adaptive Bench, dry-run MUST report the initial probes, resolved aggregate and request-level SLOs, `max_search_steps`, configured minimum rate resolution, and adaptive policy identity.

Each adaptive next case MUST be resolved from recorded prior case-level SLO evaluations according to that reported policy before it starts.

**Rationale:** One resolution path prevents dry-run, execution, and evidence from drifting. TOML-path overrides retain rapid experiment iteration without creating persistent local behavior or an untyped shell surface. Fixing frontend-component presence in the server base keeps placement stable while independently patchable Gateway and P/D Router backend identities remain explicit experimental inputs. Freezing after both integration phases means every later external action consumes an already validated, fully concrete execution rather than rediscovering configuration under changing files or defaults.

When both a base layer and an overriding layer declare the framework `settings` entry `extra_args`, the two arrays MUST compose by per-flag group last-wins merge rather than wholesale replacement. Each layer's array MUST be segmented into flag groups: a `--`-prefixed token opens a new group named by the flag text before any `=`, and following tokens without a `--` prefix belong to that group; a value token preceding any flag MUST fail workspace validation with a typed error. An overriding group MUST replace the same-named earlier group in that group's original position; groups named only by the overriding layer MUST append in override order; groups absent from the overriding layer MUST be inherited unchanged, so cases are additive over the server base and no removal path exists. A bare `--` token and every token after it MUST form one verbatim passthrough block that an overriding layer replaces as a whole. Every other `settings` array MUST keep wholesale replacement. The composed array remains subject to integration validation of InferLab-owned options, and dry-run, execution, and records MUST preserve the final composed contents. The bare `--` sentinel is a composition marker only: an integration MUST NOT emit it into the rendered engine command, and MUST append the post-sentinel tokens verbatim after the managed command tail so engine last-wins parsing applies the deliberate override. Last-wins parsing cannot retract a managed store-true flag, so when a post-sentinel token names a flag from a managed flag group the integration documents as verbatim-replaceable, the integration MUST suppress its managed rendering of that group entirely and MUST record the suppression with the rendered command; the verbatim block then owns the group's spelling.

*Since: v0.1.0*

### [RFC-0003:C-RUNTIME-WORKFLOWS] Runtime Workflows (Normative) <a id="rfc-0003c-runtime-workflows"></a>

InferLab MUST support a long-running server workflow in which an operator starts one resolved server behavior, observes its status and logs, and explicitly stops it.

InferLab MUST support a closed-loop recipe workflow in which InferLab resolves the recipe's server and effective case selection, starts it, waits for readiness, executes the workload suite, and stops the server.

Both workflows MUST use the same server and case resolution, validation, integration planning and rendering, launch, readiness, runtime-handle, and cleanup behavior.

A successfully started long-running server record MUST remain running until an explicit stop or recovery action finalizes it. Its resolved recipe identity MUST be null. A recipe record MUST preserve its recipe identity and selected server and case.

InferLab is an experiment harness, not a production supervisor. It MUST NOT automatically restart experiment servers or claim availability guarantees.

During a live start or closed-loop command, InferLab MUST attempt cleanup after handled launch, readiness, measurement, interruption, or cancellation failure. A closed-loop recipe run MUST also attempt cleanup after success. Recovery after the InferLab process or host terminates before a runtime handle is durable MAY require operator cleanup, and the record MUST NOT claim verified cleanup.

The public runtime CLI MUST provide:

- `serve start <server>`, accepting optional `--case`, `--placement`, mutually exclusive `--image` and `--external-image`, repeatable `--set`, `--local`, and `--dry-run`;
- `serve status <record>`, `serve logs <record>`, and `serve stop <record>`;
- `recipe run <recipe>`, accepting the same server realization selectors plus `--capture`;
- `bench <bench> --serve <record>`, accepting repeatable `--set`, `--capture`, and `--dry-run`.

`serve start` MUST select the named server directly. `recipe run` MUST select the server named by the recipe. Both MUST resolve exactly one effective server behavior and zero or one case identity under [RFC-0003:C-RECIPE-COMPOSITION](../rfc/RFC-0003.md#rfc-0003c-recipe-composition).

`--local` MUST be accepted only by `serve start`, `recipe run`, and `image build` among these governed runtime workflows. Server `status`, `logs`, and `stop` MUST resolve lifecycle facts solely from the named record and MUST NOT load shared workspace configuration or local bindings.

SSH execution MUST remain noninteractive while honoring the selected target’s OpenSSH configuration as the authority for connection timeout and keepalive policy. InferLab MUST NOT inject fixed connection-timeout or keepalive values that override that target configuration. An SSH child invoked inside an InferLab operation or cleanup deadline MUST remain supervised by that owner’s remaining bound.

After the resolved object is frozen and a durable record exists, real launch MUST execute stack realization checks and machine hardware probes, materialize launch files, then spawn model-serving ranks in canonical order: `serve`, or `prefill` then `decode`, with replica and rank indices ascending. When present, the one `gateway` frontend process MUST spawn after all model-serving ranks. A P/D frontend MUST bind Gateway and P/D Router to that process and spawn it exactly once. Readiness evaluation MUST begin only after every resolved process has spawned. Rollback and cleanup MUST proceed in reverse spawn order.

A Gateway-backed topology MUST NOT be reported ready until every required model-serving backend, its P/D Router when present, and its public Gateway endpoint are ready. A handled partial-start failure MUST attempt rollback of every process already started.

`serve start` and `recipe run` MAY select a successful image build record. The selected host-platform assembly substitutes for the local stack realization through the same containerized substitution used by image validation ([RFC-0007:C-IMAGE-BUILD](../rfc/RFC-0007.md#rfc-0007c-image-build)); all other server resolution, measurement, evidence, and cleanup semantics remain unchanged.

Image-backed resolution MUST reject profiling capture until this specification defines an in-container profiler contract, because a host profiler wrapping the container client does not observe the server process.

Built-image integration planning and rendering MUST execute against the selected image realization through its entrypoint and one-shot JSON contract, consuming the integration packages baked into the image. It MUST NOT require a locally installed stack environment. A failed or timed-out adapter invocation MUST NOT leave its container running.

Local bindings MAY declare positive `adapter.timeout_seconds` and `adapter.image_timeout_seconds` values for local-process and image-backed adapter invocations respectively. Omission MUST resolve to 30 seconds for a local-process invocation and 120 seconds for an image-backed invocation. The local-process deadline MUST begin immediately before spawning the adapter process in the selected stack environment. The image-backed deadline MUST begin immediately before requesting creation of the adapter container. Each deadline MUST cover the complete one-shot adapter response and process outcome, and adapter timing evidence MUST preserve its configured budget, elapsed time, and terminal cause. Adapter process or container cleanup MUST remain separately governed by [RFC-0009:C-CLEANUP-GRACE](../rfc/RFC-0009.md#rfc-0009c-cleanup-grace). Local bindings MAY also declare, only for a host whose container runtime rejects device-less container creation, one workaround device. The adapter container MUST request no device when none is declared and no capability beyond that workaround.

A built-image selection MUST be rejected before any state-affecting command or integration invocation when the record's image stack differs from the server stack, when it has no successful assembly for the launching host platform, or when the selected placement is not entirely local to the machine whose builder storage holds the image. InferLab defines no distribution of a built image between machines.

A built-image server record MUST preserve the immutable image identity, image build record, image workspace revision, and invoking workspace revision so qualification drift remains observable.

A containerized launch MUST receive every resolver- and integration-set process environment variable explicitly and MUST NOT infer that set by comparison with the ambient environment.

Each `external_images` definition MUST contain only a digest-pinned `reference` and an `integration` claim; it MUST NOT claim a stack. A declaration without an immutable digest, with an invalid integration identifier, with any additional field, or with a colliding identifier MUST be rejected at workspace load.

An external image and built-image selection MUST be mutually exclusive. External-image resolution MUST validate the claimed integration against the server stack's integration, not claim stack equality. It MUST verify by read-only probe that the digest exists in builder storage on the controller and every launch machine, MUST NOT pull it, and MUST fail a missing image naming the machine and exact pull command.

An external-image placement MAY span machines. A remote containerized launch MUST NOT require a remote workspace realization: the image replaces the serving stack environment and the remote workspace path is only a launch directory. Machine-scoped user, launch, environment pass-through, device, capability, and cache facts MUST resolve on each launch machine and enter the record.

Each declared environment pass-through value MUST be resolved on its launch machine; an absent value MUST be reported naming that machine. On a remote launch, the value MUST expand on that machine and MUST NOT enter the resolved plan, recorded command, or launch-script text. A local launch records its effective environment under the standing unredacted-record posture.

The containerized substitution MUST lower each launch machine's declared container hardware facts ([RFC-0007:C-IMAGE-BUILD](../rfc/RFC-0007.md#rfc-0007c-image-build)) into every server container: host devices, unlimited pinned-memory ulimit, and capabilities. It MUST NOT request privileged mode.

Containerized processes launched locally or over SSH MUST carry a resolver-assigned container name as a runtime handle. Cleanup verification MUST confirm removal on the launch machine; an already absent container is confirmation. A launch failure after a container may exist MUST attempt removal using that durable name. Killing only the container client MUST NOT be reported as verified server cleanup.

A built image MUST run through its activation entrypoint. An external image MUST run through an explicit command override and assumes nothing about the image's own entrypoint. External-image adapter lowering MUST use the workspace-pinned integration packages from the committed framework-free Pixi environment named `adapter`, made available to the adapter operation without treating that environment as a serving stack or requiring the serving framework locally. Resolution MUST observe and record the framework version in the external image and reject an image in which the claimed framework is not observable.

An external-image launch is not qualified by the workspace. Its record MUST preserve a distinct realization state, make no stack-check claim, and carry the declaration identifier, digest, integration claim, and observed framework version. Manual Bench admission MUST otherwise treat local, built-image, and external-image managed servers identically.

`serve start`, `recipe run`, and `bench` MUST support dry-run under [RFC-0003:C-RESOLUTION](../rfc/RFC-0003.md#rfc-0003c-resolution).

A manual `bench` MUST target one explicit managed server record, MUST NOT select an implicit latest server, and MUST reject a record not in running state or whose typed runtime handles do not identify live processes. It MUST NOT require a separate endpoint-readiness probe; endpoint request failure remains Bench failure evidence.

No more than one manual Bench may execute against one managed server at a time. Bench acceptance and `serve stop` acceptance for that server MUST be mutually exclusive. Every handled Bench terminal outcome MUST finalize its record, terminate owned measurement process groups after timeout, interruption, or cancellation, and release server-operation ownership.

A measurement client MUST have a durable process-group handle with leader start-time identity before its first experiment effect. A later run in the same workspace MUST terminate an identity-matching survivor of an unclean exit and MUST NOT signal a process group whose identity no longer matches.

Stale operation ownership MUST NOT permanently block a later Bench or stop. Recovery MUST verify that no live owner remains and preserve its outcome when an operation record exists.

This specification does not define separate serve-scoped Eval or Bench subcommands.

**Rationale:** The two server workflows differ only in who owns the server after readiness; direct server selection no longer requires a synthetic recipe. Record-only lifecycle commands remain operable from frozen evidence even if configuration changes. Deterministic spawn and reverse cleanup order make heterogeneous multi-process failures diagnosable. Built and external images reuse the same resolved server contract while keeping their distinct distribution and qualification claims honest.

*Since: v0.1.0*

### [RFC-0003:C-SERVE-TOPOLOGY] Serve Topology And Frontend Binding (Normative) <a id="rfc-0003c-serve-topology"></a>

InferLab MUST support two public server topologies: `single` and `prefill_decode`. They are product workflows, not arbitrary role or component graphs.

A resolved topology MUST distinguish logical serving components from the concrete processes that realize them. Model-serving roles MUST remain hierarchical as role, replica, then rank. Every model-serving process MUST belong to exactly one role, one replica, and one rank. Frontend processes MUST use the closed component bindings defined by this clause and MUST NOT introduce arbitrary component sets.

A `single` topology MUST contain exactly one `serve` replica and MUST NOT select a KV-transfer mechanism.

A `single` server whose base definition omits `gateway_backend` MUST expose its `serve` replica's rank-zero endpoint directly. It MUST have no Gateway, P/D Router, or frontend process.

A `single` server whose base definition declares `gateway_backend` MUST contain one logical Gateway and exactly one derived `gateway` process with component binding `[gateway]`. That process endpoint MUST be the public workload endpoint. The topology MUST have no P/D Router.

A `prefill_decode` topology MUST contain independent positive replica counts for `prefill` and `decode`, one logical Gateway, and one logical P/D Router. It MUST select `gateway_backend`, `pd_router_backend`, and KV transfer independently.

A `prefill_decode` topology MUST contain exactly one derived `gateway` process whose closed component binding is `[gateway, pd_router]`. The two logical plans MUST share that process identity, placement, runtime handle, launch command, logs, exit status, and cleanup outcome without aliasing their backend identities or effective semantics.

Each model-serving role's declared replica count MUST equal its resolved replica count. Replica identity MUST be unique within a role. Each replica MUST contain one or more ranks whose indices are unique and contiguous from zero.

Each model-serving replica MUST have exactly one rank-zero serving entry point. Nonzero ranks are headless participants and MUST NOT be treated as independently routable backends. Gateway dispatch, P/D routing, KV transfer, bootstrap, and side-channel targeting MUST use rank-zero endpoints unless a backend-specific clause explicitly defines a non-routing internal dependency.

Every derived `gateway` frontend process MUST have process-only identity with no replica or rank coordinates, have empty effective parallelism, demand zero devices, and carry no model locator. Workspace server configuration MUST NOT declare it directly.

A single model-serving replica MAY span machines through explicit local rank placement. Different roles and replicas MAY have different device counts, rank counts, machine sets, ports, settings, and parallelism. The one frontend process has exactly one placement.

Directed component links MUST distinguish public Gateway dispatch, P/D request routing, KV transfer, bootstrap, and side-channel semantics. A routed `single` topology MUST link Gateway to the sole `serve` rank-zero target. A `prefill_decode` topology MUST preserve the logical Gateway-to-P/D-Router handoff within the fused process and MUST link P/D Router to the complete prefill and decode rank-zero target sets. A link between prefill and decode sets MUST NOT imply one-to-one replica pairing; every actual target and routing policy MUST be explicit in the resolved result.

The selected integration MUST plan canonical model-serving roles and return separate Engine-role, Gateway, and P/D Router results when they apply. It MUST preserve requested replica counts and both backend identities; return complete effective behavior, whole-replica device counts, compatible co-rendering requirements, rendering sources, directed links, ports and endpoint kinds, readiness, profiler controls, server-control actions, and render inputs; and MUST NOT choose concrete model rank decomposition, machines, devices, port values, model locators, or runtime storage.

The control plane MUST apply [RFC-0002:C-LOCAL-PLACEMENT](../rfc/RFC-0002.md#rfc-0002c-local-placement), derive the closed frontend process binding from the topology, allocate ranks, machines, devices, ports, model locators, cache roots, and network facts, then supply each integration-rendered concrete allocation to final integration rendering.

The selected integration MUST render exactly one process for every supplied allocation and no additional process. It MUST preserve each model allocation's process, role, replica, and rank identity and each frontend allocation's process role and closed component binding. A control-plane-rendered frontend allocation MUST NOT be supplied to integration rendering.

The control plane MUST validate model-role identities, replica cardinality, rank continuity, frontend component presence, independent backend identities, the closed component-to-process binding, rendering sources, links, resource totals, launch dependencies, endpoint authority, and public endpoint uniqueness before the first launch.

A resolved topology MUST expose exactly one public workload endpoint: the sole `serve` rank-zero endpoint for direct single serving or the Gateway endpoint for every Gateway-backed topology. Single and prefill/decode topologies MUST use the same runtime-handle, rollback, readiness, status, logs, stop, recovery, and cleanup semantics.

The vLLM integration MUST support `prefill_decode` over Mooncake and NIXL with independent positive prefill and decode replica counts and the backend-pair obligations in [RFC-0003:C-GATEWAY-PD-ROUTER](../rfc/RFC-0003.md#rfc-0003c-gateway-pd-router).

The required logical-component, role, replica, rank, frontend-binding, allocation, and rendering shapes MUST use adapter protocol version 7 under [RFC-0006:C-INTEGRATIONS](../rfc/RFC-0006.md#rfc-0006c-integrations). An adapter advertising protocol version 6 or earlier MUST NOT emit or consume them.

**Rationale:** Gateway, P/D Router, and Engine describe responsibilities with independent backend authority; replicas describe independently routable Engine instances; ranks describe model-serving processes. The two closed frontend bindings express direct Gateway and fused P/D frontend processes without creating a general deployment graph. Independent backend selections and plans preserve the semantic boundary even when one process delivers both components.

*Since: v0.1.0*

### [RFC-0003:C-SERVE-PARALLELISM] Component-Aware Serve Parallelism (Normative) <a id="rfc-0003c-serve-parallelism"></a>

A server, its canonical model-serving roles, its cases, and invocation-scoped overrides MAY declare framework-neutral component-aware parallelism patches.

The component-aware shape MUST expose these optional positive-integer components: `outer.tensor_parallel_size`, `outer.pipeline_parallel_size`, `attention.tensor_parallel_size`, `attention.data_parallel_size`, `attention.context_parallel_size`, `experts.tensor_parallel_size`, `experts.data_parallel_size`, `experts.expert_parallel_size`, and `experts.dense_tensor_parallel_size`.

A server-level parallelism shape is only an inheritance patch for model-serving roles. For each role, resolution MUST merge server common values, server role values, selected-case common and role values, and invocation-scoped values under [RFC-0003:C-RESOLUTION](../rfc/RFC-0003.md#rfc-0003c-resolution). The resulting per-role request is the declared role shape.

An operator MUST be able to override one component without repeating unaffected components.

For every model-serving role, the selected integration MUST either preserve every explicitly declared component or reject the combination as unsupported before launch. It MUST fill every omitted component needed to return one complete positive-integer effective shape for that role.

The sole effective parallelism authority MUST be each role's complete effective shape. The integration protocol and resolved execution MUST NOT return or reconstruct a server-wide effective parallelism shape.

Every derived `gateway` frontend process role MUST have an empty effective shape and zero device count. A P/D frontend has one `gateway` process shape for both logical components.

Prefill and decode MAY resolve to different tensor, pipeline, data, context, expert, and dense tensor parallelism, different whole-replica device count, different replica counts, and different rank decompositions.

Dry-run output and records MUST preserve common and role declarations, the source of each declared component, and each role's complete effective shape.

Placement MUST consume whole-replica device count derived from each complete effective role shape.

The framework-neutral configuration and protocol MUST NOT expose framework-native flags or framework-specific parallelism algebra.

These required per-role shapes MUST use adapter protocol version 8. An adapter advertising protocol version 7 or earlier MUST NOT emit or consume them.

**Rationale:** Common values remove repetition but do not create a second effective authority. Per-role effective shapes are necessary because prefill and decode can use different card counts and decomposition, while the integration remains responsible for each framework's algebra and unsupported combinations.

*Since: v0.1.0*

### <del>[RFC-0003:C-EXPERIMENTAL-PROXY] Gateway And P/D Router Contract</del> (Normative) <a id="rfc-0003c-experimental-proxy"></a>

> **Status:** superseded
> **Superseded by:** RFC-0003:C-GATEWAY-PD-ROUTER

Superseded by [RFC-0003:C-GATEWAY-PD-ROUTER](../rfc/RFC-0003.md#rfc-0003c-gateway-pd-router).

*Since: v0.1.0*

### [RFC-0003:C-SGLANG-PREFILL-DECODE] SGLang Prefill Decode Routing (Normative) <a id="rfc-0003c-sglang-prefill-decode"></a>

The SGLang integration MUST support Mooncake and NIXL as selectable KV-transfer mechanisms for the prefill/decode topology defined by [RFC-0003:C-SERVE-TOPOLOGY](../rfc/RFC-0003.md#rfc-0003c-serve-topology).

The SGLang integration MUST support independent positive replica counts for the prefill and decode roles.

For both KV-transfer mechanisms, the SGLang integration MUST declare one control-plane-allocated bootstrap endpoint for every prefill replica.

The SGLang prefill/decode topology MUST support the independently selected backend pairs `(builtin, builtin)` and `(sglang-router, sglang-router)`. The first tuple member is `gateway_backend` and the second is `pd_router_backend`. Each pair MUST support both Mooncake and NIXL.

The SGLang integration MUST reject every unlisted Gateway/P/D Router pair during resolution before launching a process. The two backend axes MUST remain separately represented even when the selected identifiers are equal.

Selecting `(builtin, builtin)` MUST return separate Gateway and P/D Router results with `render_source = control_plane`, implementation kind `sglang`, and one fused process binding. It MUST use the InferLab-rendered proxy and MUST NOT require a SGLang Model Gateway package in the serving workspace.

Selecting `(sglang-router, sglang-router)` MUST return separate Gateway and P/D Router results with `render_source = integration` and one fused SGLang Model Gateway process from the selected stack or image realization under [RFC-0003:C-GATEWAY-PD-ROUTER](../rfc/RFC-0003.md#rfc-0003c-gateway-pd-router).

The two supported pairs MUST NOT alias one another in resolution, rendered commands, or record evidence. Gateway and P/D Router identities MUST remain separately attributable within either pair.

Both P/D Router backends MUST target only the rank-zero serving entry point of each selected prefill and decode replica.

Initial server readiness with either pair MUST wait for every configured prefill replica, every configured decode replica, the P/D Router readiness requirements, and the Gateway public endpoint to become ready.

An integration-rendered SGLang Model Gateway MUST use its worker-aware readiness endpoint, which is unsuccessful until at least one prefill and one decode worker are healthy, rather than its process-liveness endpoint.

Before reporting an SGLang Model Gateway topology ready, InferLab MUST verify through the P/D Router worker registry that every configured rank-zero prefill and decode target is registered with its expected role, every prefill target has its expected bootstrap port, and every target is healthy.

For each public completions or chat-completions request, the InferLab-rendered P/D Router MUST select one configured prefill replica and one configured decode replica.

The InferLab-rendered Gateway MUST accept the scalar-prompt completion request shape consumed by InferLab and MUST reject a prompt-array completion request before P/D dispatch.

For a chat-completions request, the InferLab-rendered Gateway and P/D Router MUST preserve the original structured message request and selected `/v1/chat/completions` path for both roles. They MUST NOT translate messages into a scalar prompt, apply completion-only prompt validation, or dispatch either phase to the completions path.

For either route, the fused implementation MUST preserve every request-body member it does not own. The P/D Router MUST inject only the selected prefill bootstrap host, bootstrap port, and one request-unique bootstrap room into the request delivered to both selected replicas.

The P/D Router MUST initiate both role requests without waiting for a prefill generation response and MUST drain the prefill response.

When the request sets `stream` to false or omits it, Gateway MUST return the complete decode response.

When the request sets `stream` to true, Gateway MUST relay the decode response incrementally while preserving its status and content type.

A prefill or decode failure observed before public response headers are sent MUST produce an HTTP status outside 200 through 299.

A prefill or decode failure observed after response streaming begins MUST terminate the public stream as failed rather than complete it successfully.

Both Gateway backends MUST expose the exact completions and chat-completions paths governed by RFC-0003:C-OPENAI-WORKLOAD-ROUTES.

Both Gateway backends MUST expose `POST /flush_cache` as the prefix-cache reset action through the public endpoint.

The corresponding P/D Router backend MUST attempt the public prefix-cache reset action on every configured prefill and decode replica.

Gateway MUST return HTTP 200 only when every target succeeds and HTTP 206 when one or more targets fail.

InferLab MUST record HTTP 206 from the public prefix-cache reset action as reset failure evidence.

Both supported pairs MUST otherwise use the common backend independence, realization, lifecycle, readiness, rollback, cleanup, and evidence requirements in [RFC-0003:C-GATEWAY-PD-ROUTER](../rfc/RFC-0003.md#rfc-0003c-gateway-pd-router).

**Rationale:** Gateway and P/D Router are separate experimental facts even though both currently supported SGLang providers fuse them into one process. The built-in implementation and SGLang Model Gateway remain complementary operator choices: a dependency-light experiment baseline and the upstream provider. SGLang uses the prefill bootstrap rendezvous for both Mooncake and NIXL, so transport selection remains independent. Registry-backed readiness proves the P/D Router target set, while Gateway remains authoritative for public routes, streaming, and cache-control responses.

*Since: v0.5.0*

### [RFC-0003:C-TENSORRT-LLM-PREFILL-DECODE] TensorRT-LLM Prefill Decode Routing (Normative) <a id="rfc-0003c-tensorrt-llm-prefill-decode"></a>

The TensorRT-LLM integration MUST support NIXL as the selectable KV-transfer mechanism for the prefill/decode topology defined by [RFC-0003:C-SERVE-TOPOLOGY](../rfc/RFC-0003.md#rfc-0003c-serve-topology).

The TensorRT-LLM integration MUST reject every other KV-transfer mechanism for this topology before launching a process.

The TensorRT-LLM integration MUST support independent positive replica counts for the prefill and decode roles.

A TensorRT-LLM prefill/decode topology MUST support the independently selected backend pairs `(builtin, builtin)` and `(trtllm-disaggregated, trtllm-disaggregated)`. The first tuple member is `gateway_backend` and the second is `pd_router_backend`.

The integration MUST reject every unlisted Gateway/P/D Router pair during resolution before launching a process. The two backend axes MUST remain separately represented even when the selected identifiers are equal.

The two supported pairs MUST NOT alias one another in resolution, rendered commands, or record evidence. Gateway and P/D Router identities MUST remain separately attributable within either pair.

Both pairs MUST declare one logical Gateway-to-P/D-Router handoff, P/D Router links to the prefill and decode roles, and one NIXL KV-transfer link from prefill to decode.

The P/D Router backends MUST NOT invent a control-plane bootstrap or side-channel endpoint when the selected TensorRT-LLM NIXL protocol exchanges its connection metadata in the context response.

Both P/D Router backends MUST target only the rank-zero serving entry point of each selected prefill and decode replica.

Each prefill and decode Engine worker MUST receive an integration-rendered launch file under [RFC-0006:C-LAUNCH-FILES](../rfc/RFC-0006.md#rfc-0006c-launch-files).

The effective Engine worker configuration MUST select the NIXL cache-transceiver backend and the Python cache-transceiver runtime.

The effective prefill-worker configuration MUST disable the overlap scheduler.

The effective KV-cache configuration of every prefill and decode worker MUST disable block reuse while the Gateway advertises no prefix-cache reset action.

An open TensorRT-LLM settings escape hatch MUST NOT override the selected cache-transceiver backend, cache-transceiver runtime, required prefill overlap setting, or required block-reuse setting.

Selecting `(builtin, builtin)` MUST return separate Gateway and P/D Router results with `render_source = control_plane`, implementation kind `trtllm`, and one fused process binding. It MUST use the InferLab-rendered TensorRT-LLM frontend and MUST NOT require the native TensorRT-LLM disaggregated server.

For each public completions or chat-completions request, the InferLab-rendered P/D Router MUST select one configured prefill replica and one configured decode replica using independent static round-robin selection.

The InferLab-rendered Gateway MUST accept the scalar-string-prompt completion request shape consumed by InferLab.

The Gateway MUST reject prompt arrays and a requested completion count other than one before dispatching a completions request to P/D Router.

The Gateway MUST accept the structured message request shape for chat completions and MUST reject a requested chat-completion count other than one. It MUST preserve messages, chat-template arguments, reasoning controls, tools, and every other request-body member it does not own. It MUST NOT translate a chat request into a completions request.

The P/D Router MUST assign each dispatched request a request-unique integer greater than or equal to `1 << 42` and MUST use that same `disagg_request_id` for its context and generation phases.

The P/D Router MUST issue the selected prefill replica a non-streaming context-only request with context-first scheduling semantics on the same selected completions or chat-completions path as the public request.

The P/D Router MUST reject a context response that has no first choice.

When the first context-response choice has finish reason `length` or `not_finished`, the P/D Router MUST reject the response unless it contains prompt-token identifiers for the selected request family, top-level usage, and a first-choice disaggregated-parameter object whose `ctx_request_id` is non-null, whose `disagg_request_id` equals the identifier assigned to the context request, and whose `first_gen_tokens` is present.

For a completions request, those prompt-token identifiers MUST be a prompt-token array. For a chat-completions request, they MUST be a `prompt_token_ids_b64` string when supplied by the context response, otherwise a prompt-token array.

When the first context-response choice has a finish reason other than `length` or `not_finished`, the P/D Router MUST NOT dispatch a decode request.

For a non-streaming public request that completes during the context phase, the P/D Router MUST remove internal disaggregated parameters and Gateway MUST return the complete context response.

For a streaming public request that completes during the context phase, the P/D Router MUST remove internal disaggregated parameters and Gateway MUST convert the complete route-specific context response into one or more valid completions or chat-completions server-sent events that preserve its generated content, choice identity, and finish reason, then emit the terminal `data: [DONE]` event without dispatching a decode request.

When a completions generation handoff is required, the P/D Router MUST replace the original prompt with the context response's prompt-token array.

When a chat-completions generation handoff is required, the P/D Router MUST preserve the original structured messages and set the generation request's `prompt_token_ids_b64` from the context response when present, otherwise its `prompt_token_ids` array. It MUST dispatch the generation phase to the selected decode replica at `/v1/chat/completions`.

The generation request MUST copy every member of the returned disaggregated-parameter object that the P/D Router does not explicitly replace.

The generation request MUST replace only `request_type`, `schedule_style`, and `ctx_usage` in that object, setting them respectively to generation-only, context-first, and the context response's top-level usage.

When the public request is non-streaming, Gateway MUST return the complete decode response.

When the public request is streaming, the P/D Router MUST keep the context request non-streaming and Gateway MUST relay the decode response incrementally while preserving its status and content type.

A context or decode failure observed before public response headers are sent MUST produce an HTTP status outside 200 through 299.

A decode failure observed after public response streaming begins MUST terminate the public stream as failed rather than complete it successfully.

Selecting `(trtllm-disaggregated, trtllm-disaggregated)` MUST return separate Gateway and P/D Router results with `render_source = integration` and one fused component binding. The selected stack or image realization MUST render one native TensorRT-LLM disaggregated server under [RFC-0003:C-GATEWAY-PD-ROUTER](../rfc/RFC-0003.md#rfc-0003c-gateway-pd-router).

The native P/D Router MUST receive a static context-first round-robin configuration containing every configured rank-zero prefill and decode target through an integration-rendered launch file under [RFC-0006:C-LAUNCH-FILES](../rfc/RFC-0006.md#rfc-0006c-launch-files).

Initial server readiness with either pair MUST wait for every configured prefill replica, every configured decode replica, the P/D Router readiness requirements, and the Gateway public endpoint to become ready.

Both Gateway backends MUST expose the exact completions and chat-completions paths governed by RFC-0003:C-OPENAI-WORKLOAD-ROUTES.

Neither Gateway backend MUST advertise a prefix-cache reset action for this workflow while the selected TensorRT-LLM serving interface exposes no action that can reset every configured prefill and decode worker.

Frontend evidence for `(builtin, builtin)` MUST record separate Gateway and P/D Router identities and versions for the InferLab-rendered frontend.

Frontend evidence for `(trtllm-disaggregated, trtllm-disaggregated)` MUST record separate backend identities, their shared fused process binding, and the TensorRT-LLM integration adapter version.

Both supported pairs MUST otherwise use the common backend independence, realization, lifecycle, readiness, rollback, cleanup, and evidence requirements in [RFC-0003:C-GATEWAY-PD-ROUTER](../rfc/RFC-0003.md#rfc-0003c-gateway-pd-router).

**Rationale:** TensorRT-LLM context-first disaggregation is a two-stage P/D Router protocol for both standard OpenAI request forms, while Gateway retains the public route, validation, response, and streaming contract. The context response carries prompt tokens, the first generated token, usage, and opaque connection metadata needed to construct the generation-only request. The built-in fused frontend is therefore a bounded protocol adapter rather than the concurrent bootstrap implementation used by SGLang. The native disaggregated server remains separately selectable on both backend axes so operators can compare an InferLab-rendered baseline with upstream orchestration while records retain the Gateway/P/D Router semantic split. NIXL carries its dynamic endpoint in response metadata, so requiring a bootstrap or side-channel port would record and allocate a topology that does not exist. Disabling block reuse provides repeatable measurement isolation while no composed reset action exists.

*Since: v0.6.0*

### [RFC-0003:C-TOKENSPEED-PREFILL-DECODE] TokenSpeed Prefill Decode Routing (Normative) <a id="rfc-0003c-tokenspeed-prefill-decode"></a>

The TokenSpeed integration MUST support the prefill/decode topology defined by [RFC-0003:C-SERVE-TOPOLOGY](../rfc/RFC-0003.md#rfc-0003c-serve-topology).

The topology's Gateway backend, P/D Router backend, and KV-transfer mechanism MUST remain independently selected and independently recorded.

The TokenSpeed integration MUST accept Mooncake as the KV-transfer mechanism for this topology and MUST reject every other mechanism during resolution before launching a process.

The TokenSpeed integration MUST support independent positive replica counts for the prefill and decode roles.

A TokenSpeed prefill/decode topology MUST accept the independently selected backend pair `(tokenspeed-smg, tokenspeed-smg)`. The first tuple member is `gateway_backend` and the second is `pd_router_backend`.

The integration MUST reject every other Gateway/P/D Router pair during resolution before launching a process in this RFC version. The two selected backend facts MUST remain distinct even though both currently name SMG.

The topology MUST declare one logical Gateway-to-P/D-Router handoff, P/D Router links to the prefill and decode roles, one Mooncake KV-transfer link from prefill to decode, and one control-plane-allocated bootstrap endpoint for every prefill replica.

P/D routing, KV transfer, and bootstrap targeting MUST use only the rank-zero serving entry point of each selected prefill and decode replica.

Each rendered prefill Engine worker MUST expose a TokenSpeed gRPC serving endpoint and MUST receive the prefill disaggregation role, the Mooncake transfer backend, and its allocated bootstrap endpoint.

Each rendered decode Engine worker MUST expose a TokenSpeed gRPC serving endpoint and MUST receive the decode disaggregation role and the Mooncake transfer backend.

An open TokenSpeed settings escape hatch MUST NOT override the resolved disaggregation role, KV-transfer backend, model, served endpoint, process topology, parallelism, or allocated bootstrap endpoint.

Selecting `(tokenspeed-smg, tokenspeed-smg)` MUST return separate Gateway and P/D Router results with `render_source = integration` and one fused component binding. The selected stack or image realization MUST render one native SMG process under [RFC-0003:C-GATEWAY-PD-ROUTER](../rfc/RFC-0003.md#rfc-0003c-gateway-pd-router).

The SMG P/D Router result MUST enable prefill/decode routing and receive a static target list containing every configured rank-zero prefill gRPC endpoint paired with its bootstrap endpoint and every configured rank-zero decode gRPC endpoint.

The SMG P/D Router MUST use independent round-robin prefill and decode policies.

Initial server readiness MUST wait for every configured prefill replica, every configured decode replica, the SMG P/D Router readiness requirements, and the SMG Gateway public endpoint to become ready.

Before reporting the topology ready, InferLab MUST verify through the SMG P/D Router worker registry that every configured rank-zero gRPC target is registered with its expected role, every prefill target has its expected bootstrap port, and every target is healthy.

The SMG Gateway MUST expose the exact completions and chat-completions paths governed by RFC-0003:C-OPENAI-WORKLOAD-ROUTES and MUST preserve the selected request form through its P/D Router handoff. The SMG mapping MUST preserve structured chat messages and every supported unowned request member in its worker request; a member the mapping cannot represent MUST produce an explicit non-2xx public rejection rather than be discarded.

The SMG Gateway MUST expose `POST /flush_cache` as its public prefix-cache reset action.

The SMG P/D Router MUST attempt that action on every configured prefill and decode worker. Gateway MUST report success only when every target succeeds.

Frontend evidence MUST preserve separate `tokenspeed-smg` Gateway and P/D Router identities, their shared fused process binding, each rendering-source fact, the independent round-robin P/D policy, every rank-zero gRPC target and bootstrap endpoint, the public endpoint, and the TokenSpeed integration adapter version.

KV-transfer evidence and rendered Engine commands MUST preserve Mooncake independently from both frontend backend facts.

The topology MUST otherwise use the common backend independence, realization, lifecycle, readiness, rollback, cleanup, and evidence requirements in [RFC-0003:C-GATEWAY-PD-ROUTER](../rfc/RFC-0003.md#rfc-0003c-gateway-pd-router).

**Rationale:** SMG currently realizes Gateway and P/D Router in one process, while Mooncake owns KV movement between selected Engines. Treating those as three independent selected and recorded facts keeps the experiment model truthful and permits a later Gateway or P/D Router replacement without renaming SMG into an ownership category. TokenSpeed's packaged gRPC servicer is the stable Engine boundary consumed by SMG, and registry-backed readiness proves the complete P/D target set while InferLab retains placement and lifecycle authority.

*Since: v0.7.0*

### [RFC-0003:C-OPENAI-WORKLOAD-ROUTES] OpenAI Workload Routes (Normative) <a id="rfc-0003c-openai-workload-routes"></a>

Every supported public server endpoint MUST expose one completions route and one chat-completions route.

The completions route MUST be `/v1/completions`. The chat-completions route MUST be `/v1/chat/completions`.

The integration endpoint contract MUST declare both named paths. Resolution, dry-run output, server records, and measurement client inputs MUST preserve those declared path values and MUST NOT reconstruct either path from the other.

A direct `single` topology MUST expose both routes through the rank-zero endpoint of its sole `serve` replica. Every topology with a Gateway MUST expose both routes only through that Gateway. A P/D Router MUST NOT be a public endpoint authority.

Every Gateway backend that InferLab reports as supporting a topology MUST preserve both paths through its selected Engine or P/D Router handoff without translating a chat request into a completions request or a completions request into a chat request.

Before internal handoff, Gateway MUST preserve each request-body member it does not own or reject the public request with a non-2xx response that retains the backend diagnostic. An integration MUST NOT remove a member to compensate for the selected Gateway or P/D Router. A Gateway backend that silently discards an unowned member MUST NOT be reported as supporting or qualified for the affected request workflow.

A P/D Router MUST preserve the selected route and every unowned request member across prefill and decode dispatch unless its backend-specific handoff contract explicitly replaces that member. It MUST report a handoff incompatibility to Gateway as a failure and MUST NOT silently translate or discard the request.

An InferLab-rendered Gateway MUST preserve every public request member except a member that its specified handoff protocol explicitly replaces. It MUST return the selected route's framework response shape and streaming protocol.

An InferLab-rendered Gateway MUST NOT interpret, normalize, remove, or rename sampling, logprob, reasoning, chat-template, tool, or other framework request members that its handoff protocol does not own.

A framework and topology MUST be reported as qualified for a route only when a real public-route execution record demonstrates that exact route, model, integration revision, Gateway backend, P/D Router backend when present, frontend component binding when present, KV-transfer selection when present, and topology. Source availability or qualification of the other route MUST NOT establish that claim.

**Rationale:** Generative measurements need the model server's real chat encoding and reasoning controls, while likelihood scoring and the lowest-level smoke retain completions semantics. Two closed, named routes cover those concrete workflows without introducing an arbitrary endpoint registry. Gateway owns the public protocol boundary; P/D Router owns only the internal phase handoff. Preserving both the route and unowned body members keeps that separation observable across direct and fused serving.

*Since: v0.9.1*

### [RFC-0003:C-GATEWAY-PD-ROUTER] Gateway And P/D Router Contract (Normative) <a id="rfc-0003c-gateway-pd-router"></a>

Gateway and P/D Router MUST be separate logical components. Gateway owns the public workload boundary when present. P/D Router owns prefill/decode target selection and phase orchestration. Neither component owns placement, concrete endpoint allocation, process lifecycle, cleanup, or authoritative records; InferLab retains those authorities.

Integration planning MUST return separate `gateway` and `pd_router` results whenever the selected topology requires them. It MUST NOT return a routing-ownership union or the protocol-v6 `direct`, `inferlab_builtin`, or `integration_native` ownership variants.

Each returned frontend component result MUST preserve its independently selected backend identity, implementation identity and observable version, complete effective settings, readiness requirements, controls, links, endpoint requirements, render inputs, and one `render_source` of `control_plane` or `integration`. `render_source` means only which bounded implementation renders the accepted concrete allocation into a launch command. It MUST NOT be interpreted as process-lifecycle, placement, endpoint, cleanup, or evidence ownership.

A direct `single` server MUST omit both frontend component results and expose the sole `serve` replica's rank-zero endpoint.

A routed `single` server MUST return exactly one Gateway result matching the effective `gateway_backend`, MUST omit P/D Router, and MUST bind Gateway to one derived zero-device `gateway` process with component binding `[gateway]`. Gateway MUST target only the `serve` replica's rank-zero endpoint.

InferLab MUST NOT report a Gateway backend as supporting `single` solely from this generic contract. Routed-single support MUST have a backend-specific contract for Engine target compatibility, rendering source, readiness, both public-route semantics, and server-control behavior before it can be reported as supported or qualified.

A `prefill_decode` server MUST return one Gateway result matching the effective `gateway_backend` and one P/D Router result matching the effective `pd_router_backend`. Those backend selections and the KV-transfer mechanism MUST remain independently selected, validated, and recorded.

The selected Gateway/P/D Router backend pair MUST declare fused compatibility. An unsupported integration, topology, backend identity, backend pair, or KV-transfer mechanism MUST fail resolution before any process launches. Topology alone MUST NOT silently select either backend.

Both P/D frontend component results MUST declare the same rendering source and compatible co-rendering requirements. The control plane MUST derive one zero-device `gateway` allocation with component binding `[gateway, pd_router]`. The selected renderer MUST return one process and one command for that allocation. Gateway and P/D Router MUST share the process identity and lifecycle evidence while retaining separate logical backend identities, settings, policies, readiness obligations, controls, and versions.

For `render_source = control_plane`, the component result MUST name one closed InferLab implementation kind supported by the selected backend and topology. For the currently specified built-in P/D implementations, the closed kinds are `vllm_mooncake`, `vllm_nixl`, `sglang`, and `trtllm`. InferLab MUST render the corresponding frontend allocation and MUST NOT supply it to `render_serve`.

For `render_source = integration`, the selected integration MUST render the allocation from the chosen stack or image realization. The control plane MUST place it through the same placement authority as every other process and MUST supply the concrete allocation to `render_serve`. An integration-rendered frontend process MAY run remotely.

One stack realization, image, or integration package MAY supply Engine, Gateway, and P/D Router implementations. Co-delivery MUST NOT merge their logical identities. A fused process MAY implement two independently named backends only when the selected stack or image realization declares and validates that exact pair.

An integration MUST NOT advertise a Gateway backend unless it can validate settings, target compatibility, public endpoint semantics, readiness, public controls, implementation identity, and rendering requirements. It MUST NOT advertise a P/D Router backend unless it can validate settings, declare complete prefill and decode target semantics and policy, declare bootstrap or registry requirements, identify its internal handoff contract, and co-render it with a compatible Gateway backend.

Every Gateway and P/D Router target set MUST use only rank-zero serving entry points. Component links MUST NOT imply replica pairing; the planned policy and complete target sets are authoritative.

InferLab MUST allocate every concrete endpoint and retain lifecycle authority for every frontend process regardless of rendering source. Commands, environment, logs, readiness, durable handles, failures, rollback, cleanup, and component-to-process bindings MUST have the same evidence guarantees as model-serving processes.

A Gateway-backed topology MUST NOT report readiness until every model-serving backend required by the selected policy, the P/D Router when present, and the public Gateway endpoint are ready. Eval and Bench MUST attach only to the public workload endpoint.

When a public completions or chat-completions request sets `stream` to `true`, Gateway MUST make each complete route-native streaming event available to the public client without waiting for a later event or upstream body completion. This requirement applies independently of HTTP transport chunk boundaries. Gateway MUST preserve the successful upstream response status and content type.

An upstream failure observed before public response headers are sent MUST produce an HTTP status outside 200 through 299. An upstream failure observed after public streaming begins MUST terminate the public stream as failed rather than complete it successfully.

InferLab-provided baseline frontends MAY use static routing over configured ready backends. They MUST NOT be required to provide automatic restart, degraded-backend recovery, backend eviction, minimum-ready capacity, or production availability guarantees.

The vLLM integration MUST support the independently recorded backend pairs `(builtin, builtin)` and `(vllm-router, vllm-router)` over both Mooncake and NIXL. The first tuple member is `gateway_backend` and the second is `pd_router_backend`. The `builtin` pair MUST use `render_source = control_plane` and the corresponding closed vLLM implementation kind. The `vllm-router` pair MUST use `render_source = integration`. The integration MUST reject every unlisted cross-pair during resolution before launching a process in this RFC version.

Frontend evidence MUST preserve the effective Gateway backend, P/D Router backend with explicit absence when it does not apply, both implementation identities and versions, each rendering source, effective Gateway public behavior, effective P/D routing policy, KV-transfer selection, every target, internal link and endpoint, component-to-process binding, public endpoint, commands, and integration version when integration rendering applies. A P/D frontend process MUST be recorded once and referenced by both logical component records; evidence MUST NOT duplicate its allocation or lifecycle outcome.

**Rationale:** Protocol v7 names the real semantic boundaries instead of calling a rendering decision ownership. Independent Gateway and P/D Router selections make public API behavior and phase orchestration separately replaceable experimental facts. The fused P/D binding matches every currently demonstrated provider without promoting arbitrary deployment graphs. InferLab remains the only runtime authority, and KV movement remains a third independent mechanism. Incremental public delivery is part of Gateway correctness because client-observed TTFT and token spacing cease to describe generation when a frontend buffers the stream to completion.

*Since: v0.11.0*

### [RFC-0003:C-SERVE-CONTEXT-PARALLELISM] Serve Context Parallelism Semantics (Normative) <a id="rfc-0003c-serve-context-parallelism"></a>

A declared `attention.context_parallel_size` expresses one framework-neutral context-parallel degree for attention under [RFC-0003:C-SERVE-PARALLELISM](../rfc/RFC-0003.md#rfc-0003c-serve-parallelism).

For a `single` topology, context parallelism MUST NOT increase any role's whole-replica device count: the integration MUST lower the declared degree only to context-parallel mechanisms that subdivide the role's existing device set. For a `prefill_decode` topology, the `prefill` role MAY lower the declared degree to a prefill context-parallel mechanism that multiplies that role's whole-replica device count, and the integration MUST then derive that role's device count from the framework's algebra; the `decode` role's context parallelism MUST NOT increase its whole-replica device count.

When one declared degree activates several concrete framework mechanisms, the integration MUST render every activated mechanism into the role's command so the record preserves them, and MUST NOT activate a device-count-multiplying mechanism outside the `prefill` role of a `prefill_decode` topology.

Applicability constraints that depend on model internals such as attention architecture or head counts, on hardware generation, or on the framework's runtime kernel or backend selection are owned by the framework. The integration MUST NOT inspect model artifacts, hardware, or framework installations to pre-validate them; its own validation of a declared parallelism shape is limited to arithmetic over the declared components. A framework's rejection of an unsupported combination surfaces as a recorded launch failure.

**Rationale:** One declared degree keeps the neutral surface minimal while engines split context parallelism into incompatible prefill and decode mechanisms. The device-count rule keeps `single` requests resource-predictable and confines device-multiplying prefill context parallelism to the `prefill` role it accelerates. Model-internal applicability moves with framework releases and fork behavior, so the framework, not the integration, owns it; the integration's records preserve what was declared and rendered, and captured launch output preserves the framework's own verdict.

*Since: v0.14.0*

## Changelog

### v0.15.0 (2026-08-21)

Verbatim extra-args may suppress non-retractable managed flag groups

#### Added

- when a post-sentinel token names a flag in a documented verbatim-replaceable group (store-true flags last-wins cannot retract), the integration suppresses the managed rendering of the whole group and records the suppression; the verbatim block owns the group spelling

### v0.14.1 (2026-08-21)

Strip the extra-args passthrough sentinel from rendered engine commands

#### Changed

- the undeclared capture_finalization_deadline_seconds default follows the resolved capture mechanism: 300 s for managed collection, 3600 s for engine trace, whose close dispatch and flush wait share the one global finalization budget

#### Fixed

- the bare '--' in composed extra_args is a composition marker that integrations must not emit into the rendered engine command; post-sentinel tokens are appended verbatim after the managed tail (argparse-based engine launchers reject a literal '--')
